name: Malware Scanner by Antivirus.ai – Shieldlume Security
author: Plugins.shop

sections.description:
Shieldlume Security by Antivirus.ai, from Plugins.shop, is a WordPress antivirus and malware scanner with file integrity, login protection, hardening and reviewed Free recovery. Local tools need no account, paid key or AI.

Free & Pro interface demo | Owner guide | Compare editions

WordPress malware scanning

  • Resumable checks of eligible core, plugins, themes, uploads and selected database content.
  • The harmless EICAR test marker across extensions, including .txt/.com, plus a small versioned catalog of five exact PHP webshell fingerprints.
  • Separate PHP/JavaScript heuristics, suspicious execution chains and PHP hidden in images; modified variants can be missed.
  • Automatic clear-origin WordPress.org verification after one global opt-in, using official metadata/checksums or exact-version packages. Ambiguous identities need review.
  • Added/modified/missing files grouped by plugin, theme or folder. Critical/high/review counts describe the current selection.
  • Low priority for ordinary font, image, CSS and text differences; higher priority for executable or PHP-containing files. A checksum difference alone is not infection proof.
  • Hash-bound Mark as expected decisions and explicit Ignore folder rules. Changed bytes become reviewable again; exclusions stay visible.

Free recovery and hardening

Restore official copy uses verified exact-version bytes; Quarantine removes an approved eligible source only after authenticating its encrypted backup. A local restore index keeps originals; completed/failed/cancelled owned backups become eligible for bounded daily cleanup after 30 days. Active, uncertain and unknown objects stay for review. Recovery requires POSIX ownership, Sodium, fsync, private storage and safe atomic publication; host setup may be needed. Boot/configuration and Shieldlume control-plane quarantine are refused.

18 hardening controls and five manual audits cover file editing, uploads PHP, XML-RPC, versions, user enumeration, headers, configuration access, directory listing, passwords, debug display, permissions and minor core updates. Review warnings before Apply. Undo removes only the exact owned change; unsupported server actions show manual instructions. Before header Apply, a same-origin browser response check refuses headers already supplied there, including server/CDN headers. JavaScript is required for this check; Undo remains available without it. Use one owner per header and recheck after host changes.

Sign-in, firewall and notifications

Fresh installs enable five failed sign-ins per account in 15 minutes, with backoff, and Observe firewall. A dismissible notice offers Switch firewall to Block. Upgrades retain settings. Trusted administrator exemptions/recovery do not bypass authentication or enrolled 2FA; early filtering needs host review.

Free includes authenticator 2FA, recovery codes, password plus passkey, optional administrator policies, endpoint controls, email alerts/digests and findings/coverage exports. Known conflicts may suspend login limits. Filtering covers supported WordPress requests, without CDN/DDoS protection.

Compatible Logged.ai supplies nearby local activity, subject to permissions/retention; context does not prove causation. Its finding-page installation suggestion is dismissible. Separate Pro adds automation, investigations, reports and optional connected AI using the same scanner. Free never downloads paid code.

Related plugins by Plugins.shop

  • Logged.ai – activity log: supported logins and site changes.
  • ClickClue – session replay: visitor journeys with privacy controls.

Separate optional tools. More from Plugins.shop.

External services and privacy

Connections require permission/configuration; viewing panels sends nothing. No usage/conversion telemetry. Privacy/operator | Terms. Full retention/withdrawal: docs/privacy-and-services.md, privacy.txt and online disclosure.

  • Antivirus.ai welcome/newsletter: unchecked choices send domain, WordPress/PHP/language, or email/edition to https://antivirus.ai/newsletter-api/v1/plugin-welcome/ . Consented reports refresh weekly or on edition changes; no source/findings/customer records. Email needs confirmation; stop sharing and unsubscribe separately. Sharing privacy, email privacy.
  • WordPress.org: permitted identity/checksum/package jobs send component/version, core locale where relevant, server IP/timing. Comparison stays local; no source upload. Privacy.
  • Wordfence Intelligence: permitted/configured requests use your API credential/server connection, without source uploads. Saving a token does not enable requests. Terms, privacy.
  • Signed indicators: a configured publisher receives protocol/version metadata and server IP for permitted updates, not inventory/samples. Destination/policy appears before enabling. Bundled signatures need no download.
  • Local ClamAV: eligible bytes go to a protected host daemon; the host manages definitions, FreshClam requests and logs. Guidance.
  • Emerging Threats: permitted https://rules.emergingthreats.net/blockrules/compromised-ips.txt downloads normally run every 12 hours. Provider sees server IP/timing, not visitor IPs/content; matching is local. Licence, privacy.
  • Pwned Passwords: permitted supported checks send five SHA-1 prefix characters and server IP/timing to https://api.pwnedpasswords.com , never password/full hash/username/email. Service, privacy.
  • Exposure checks: permitted HTTPS probes contact this site’s public address. Its host/CDN sees selected paths and server IP/timing; up to 512 response bytes are compared transiently, without Antivirus.ai upload.
  • Email: selected alerts/tests send content and recipient through your WordPress mail provider. Acceptance is not confirmed delivery; interrupted/uncertain sends need review.

Logged.ai uses its public local API/route with current viewing permissions, no direct table access/off-site request. Logged.ai controls retention. Free sends no Pro/AI request; Pro services require separate consent/access and cannot approve repairs. Service privacy, terms, AI privacy.

Protect exports/recovery and handle provider records, backups and withdrawals separately. Self-service software, without managed cleanup or response-time guarantees. Support.

Source code and third-party notices

Readable source/assets are bundled. Authentication/QR builds and MIT licences: vendor/auth/NOTICE.md. Space Grotesk OFL: assets/fonts/OFL.txt. Local signature fingerprints and provenance: data/local-signatures.json; no executable specimen is shipped.
sections.installation:
1. Keep an independent backup. Install on single-site WordPress 6.8+ with 64-bit PHP 8.1+. Use a security-supported PHP branch.
  2. Open Shieldlume Security. File scanning needs canonical local POSIX paths; Multisite, symlinked components, Windows drive/UNC paths and FTP replacement are unsupported.
  3. Start a scan. Visible-page batches, Continue scanning and traffic-dependent WP-Cron resume approved work. Activation starts no scan/provider request.
  4. Review evidence and coverage. Enable official references if wanted; read warnings before Block, hardening or recovery.
sections.faq:
What is enabled by default?

Fresh installs use Observe firewall and failure-based login limits; upgrades keep settings/login policy. External permissions remain off until enabled. Global WordPress.org permission enables automatic clear-origin verification, without enabling other providers.

Are signatures comprehensive?

No. EICAR is a harmless antivirus test, and five exact webshell fingerprints cover only those variants. Heuristics remain separate. Review coverage; no clean-site guarantee is offered.

Does Free delete malware automatically?

No. Scans do not alter source. Recovery requires reviewed administrator approval and verified encrypted originals first. Original-byte restore can reintroduce flagged code; official restore does not upgrade vulnerable software. Completed/failed/cancelled owned backups become eligible for bounded daily cleanup after 30 days; missed cron can delay deletion, and uncertain records stay retained.

Why can a finished scan have limits?

Structural checks use an adaptive 2/8/16 MiB policy with an override. Hashing/streaming are separate; changed, excluded or unfinished content is not clean. Optional ClamAV has a 2 MiB limit. Methods.

Does uninstall erase data?

Keep is default. Guarded removal preserves needed recovery keys/indexes and managed hardening journals. Reinstall can resume sharing; stop sharing/unsubscribe separately. See docs/data-uninstall.md.
sections.changelog:
1.2.5

  • Record a requested email test separately from protection-setting changes in Activity. Queue acceptance does not claim inbox delivery.
  • Keep the shared Free/Pro release number aligned; existing scan evidence and protection choices are retained.

1.2.4

  • Keep scan summary pointers compact while retaining detailed per-file coverage in the scan report.
  • Account for clean inactive file cache within container memory limits and retry transient resource-limited files once in a fresh batch. Real limits remain visible.
  • Report zero-assessed checks as no_content_assessed in schema 3 JSON and local reports; preserve finding priority.
  • Avoid false missing-wakeup errors when another worker has already scheduled the scan.
  • Give plugin form controls unique IDs without changing security-field names or permissions.

1.2.3

  • Routes the setup notice to the firewall review form instead of switching to Block in one click, and avoids duplicate WordPress form IDs.
  • Keeps broad site scan results separate from targeted checks, including checks that assess no files.
  • Clarifies the saved scan summary and its relationship to Activity receipts.

1.2.2

  • Reopen a reviewed finding without removing its evidence; reject stale or invalid review actions.
  • Show the next requested scheduled wake-up in UTC and explain that WordPress cron may run late.
  • Refresh the complete saved dashboard after a scan ends. Preserve unfinished input and offer an explicit results link when automatic refresh is unsafe.
  • Label human-readable scan, finding and activity times explicitly as UTC while preserving machine-readable timestamps.

1.2.1

  • Fix Get Pro navigation under strict form security policies; keep optional local task saving separate.
  • Check the browser’s final same-origin frontend response before enabling a response-header control. Refuse already supplied headers, failed checks and stale receipts; retain Undo without JavaScript.
  • Preserve existing PHP-queued headers and document the limits of checking one response before later host/CDN changes.
  • Serve bundled scanner methods through an authenticated fixed-document view when direct Markdown files are blocked.
  • Clarify related local-task, browser-check and privacy guidance.

1.2.0

  • Add fresh-install Observe firewall and five-failure backoff; preserve upgrade choices.
  • Bundle EICAR/five exact webshell signatures; automate clear official origins after opt-in.
  • Group/prioritize findings; add expected hashes and folder exclusions.
  • Add reviewed Free encrypted recovery, 18 hardening controls, five audits and local Logged.ai context.
  • Support PHP 8.1+; update privacy, recovery and compatibility guidance.
  • Fix early translation loading after saved hardening controls while preserving pre-init protection.

Earlier releases: bundled changelog.txt.
